submitted.rationale: Index 12 (Co0.53Sb0.47) gave the only positive EQE (0.0049%). The mixed trirutile+spinel midpoint beat both single-phase regions. All values are near the noise floor, so the Co-Sb line appears to be a weak photoanode under 2.1 eV light.

rejected.reason: CoSb2O6 trirutile: stable on the MACE hull but measured EQE -0.0042%
Co7Sb2O12 spinel region: MEGNet gap 1.44 eV should absorb, but measured EQE -0.0007%

consultations.verdict: Support (moderate): trirutile CoSb2O6 is on the MACE hull (Ehull 0), so index 18 (Co 0.326) should be near phase-pure. MEGNet HSE gap 0.37 eV is likely an underestimate for this Co2+ d-d system; any gap below 2.1 eV permits absorption, so it does not argue against. Measure 18 as the anchor.

Support: Co7Sb2O12 spinel (Co 0.778) is near-hull (0.03 eV/atom) with MEGNet HSE gap 1.44 eV < 2.1 eV photon energy, so it should absorb. Index 5 (Co 0.765) sits at that composition. Trirutile at index 18 gave ~0 EQE, so pivot to Co-rich side.

Weak support: Co2Sb2O7 at 1:1 is metastable (Ehull 0.19), so mid-line films are likely a trirutile+spinel mixture. MEGNet gap 1.12 eV absorbs at 2.1 eV. The two single-phase endpoints (18, 5) gave ~0 EQE, so the unexplored mixed-phase midpoint (possible heterojunction) is the best remaining bet and matches the GP's top-uncertainty region.
